cues.zh: 我当时在Agenda 2000大会上，

cues.en: and, one of the people who was there was Craig Mundy, who is some kind of high mucky muck at Microsoft.
cues.zh: 在场的人里有Craig Mundy，他在微软算是个高层人物。

cues.en: I think vice president of consumer products or something like that.
cues.zh: 我记得是消费产品副总裁之类的职位。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 然后

cues.en: I hadn't actually met him. I I bumped into him in an at an elevator... In an elevator.
cues.zh: 我其实之前没见过他。我是在电梯里碰到他的……就在电梯里。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 然后

cues.zh: 我看了看他的工牌，说，我看你在微软工作。

cues.en: And he looked back at me and said, oh, yeah. And what do you do?
cues.zh: 他回看了我一眼，说，哦，是啊。那你是做什么的？

cues.en: And I thought he seemed just as as some sort of a tad dismissive. I mean, here's the archetypal, you know, guy
cues.zh: 我觉得他看起来也有点儿不屑。你知道，他就是那种典型的

cues.en: looking at a scruffy hacker.
cues.zh: 盯着邋遢黑客看的家伙。

cues.en: And so I gave him the thousand yard stare and said, I'm your worst nightmare.
cues.zh: 于是我直勾勾地盯着他，说：“我就是你最可怕的噩梦。”

cues.en: For most of its short but colorful history, the computer industry has been dominated by the Windows operating system. But that could soon change as Windows faces a strong challenge from Linux.
cues.zh: 在短暂却丰富多彩的历史中，计算机行业大多由 Windows 操作系统主导。但随着 Linux 发起强劲挑战，这种局面很快可能改变。

cues.en: Silicon Valley has long been the place to develop new technology,
cues.zh: 长期以来，硅谷一直都是研发新技术、

cues.en: start new companies,
cues.zh: 创办新公司、

cues.en: and get really rich.
cues.zh: 以及发大财的圣地。

cues.en: Now The Valley is the front line in revolution fighting for that most politically incorrect of ideas,
cues.zh: 如今，硅谷成了一场革命的最前线，这场革命旨在捍卫一个在政治上极不正确的理念——

cues.en: individual freedom.
cues.zh: 个人自由。

cues.en: Day and night, a loose confederation of hackers and programmer zaps bits and pieces of computer code around the world as it builds the tools to set computer users free.
cues.zh: 日以继夜，一个由黑客和程序员组成的松散同盟将一段段计算机代码发送到世界各地，打造出让计算机用户获得自由的工具。

cues.en: Using open information and the free exchange of technology to achieve its goals, this revolution began in the nineteen eighties with the free software movement and the GNU project and now is most commonly associated with Linux and the open source movement.
cues.zh: 这场革命旨在通过信息公开和技术自由交流来实现目标，它始于 20 世纪 80 年代的自由软件运动和 GNU 项目，如今人们最常将其与 Linux 以及开源运动联系在一起。

cues.en: We do have one sector that is taking off today. It is the Linux related sector. I thought this might be a good opportunity to say, What is Linux?
cues.zh: 我们确实有一个领域正在蓬勃发展，那就是与Linux相关的领域。我想这可能是个好机会，来说说什么是Linux？

cues.en: And I'll answer this question for you. Many of you probably already know, but there are 12,000,000 users out there. A computer operating system developed by hundreds of programmers collaborating on the Internet. A challenge to Microsoft Windows NT. Very popular for its speed,
cues.zh: 我来为你解答这个问题。你们中许多人可能已经知道，但有1200万用户在使用它。这是一个由数百名程序员在互联网上合作开发的计算机操作系统。它对微软Windows NT构成了挑战。因其速度快而非常受欢迎，

cues.en: and so this is what the craze is about.
cues.zh: 这就是这股热潮的由来。

cues.en: To kind of explain what Linux is, you have to explain what an operating system is. And the thing about an operating system is that you... I mean, you're not... Never ever supposed to see it because
cues.zh: 要解释 Linux 是什么，得先解释什么是操作系统。操作系统有个特点：你……我是说，你不应该……绝对不应该看到它，因为

cues.en: nobody really uses an operating system. People use
cues.zh: 其实没人会直接使用操作系统。人们使用的是

cues.en: programs Uh-huh. On their computer.
cues.zh: 电脑上的程序。嗯。

cues.en: And the only mission in life of an operating system is to help those programs run.
cues.zh: 操作系统存在的唯一目的，就是帮助这些程序运行。

cues.en: So an operating system never does anything on its own.
cues.zh: 所以操作系统从来不会自己做任何事。

cues.en: It's only waiting for the programs to ask for certain resources
cues.zh: 它只是在等待程序来请求某些资源，

cues.en: or
cues.zh: 或者

cues.en: or ask
cues.zh: 或者请求

cues.en: for a certain file on the on the disc or ask for the programs to connect them to the outside world. And then the operating system comes steps in and and tries to make it easy for people to write programs.
cues.zh: 磁盘上的某个文件，或是请求将程序连接到外网。这时操作系统就会介入，尽力让大家编写程序变得更容易。

cues.en: Open source is a way for people to collaborate
cues.zh: 开源是一种协作方式，

cues.en: on software without being encumbered by all of problems of intellectual
cues.zh: 让人们能在开发软件时摆脱知识产权带来的

cues.en: property,
cues.zh: 各种麻烦，

cues.en: having to negotiate contracts
cues.zh: 不再需要

cues.en: every time you buy a piece of software,
cues.zh: 每次购买软件都去谈合同，

cues.en: have a lot of lawyers involved.
cues.zh: 也不用牵扯一大堆律师。

cues.en: In general, we just wanna get the software to work,
cues.zh: 一般来说，我们只是想让软件能跑起来，

cues.en: and we want to be able to have people contribute fixes to that, etcetera.
cues.zh: 并且希望能让人们贡献修复等等。

cues.en: So we sort of sacrifice some of the intellectual
cues.zh: 所以我们某种程度上牺牲了一些知识

cues.en: property rights and just let the whole world use the software.
cues.zh: 产权，让全世界都能使用这个软件。

cues.en: Before there could be Linux, there was Richard Stallman and the free software movement.
cues.zh: 在Linux出现之前，有Richard Stallman和自由软件运动。

cues.en: I mean, think of Richard Stallman as the
cues.zh: 我是说，把Richard Stallman看作

cues.en: great philosopher.
cues.zh: 伟大的哲学家。

cues.en: Right?
cues.zh: 对吧？

cues.en: And think of me as the engineer.
cues.zh: 把我当作工程师。

cues.en: Richard Stallman is the founding father of the free software movement.
cues.zh: Richard Stallman 是自由软件运动的开创者。

cues.en: Through his efforts to build the GNU operating system, he created the legal, philosophical,
cues.zh: 他致力于打造 GNU 操作系统，为自由软件运动奠定了法律、哲学

cues.en: and technological foundation for the free software movement.
cues.zh: 和技术基础。

cues.en: Without these contributions,
cues.zh: 没有这些贡献，

cues.en: it's unlikely that Linux and open source would have evolved into their current forms today.
cues.zh: Linux 和开源软件很可能不会发展成今天的样子。

cues.en: I joined the MIT artificial intelligence lab in 1971.
cues.zh: 我于 1971 年加入麻省理工学院人工智能实验室。

cues.en: I joined
cues.zh: 我加入了

cues.en: a thriving community
cues.zh: 一个充满活力的社群，

cues.en: of hackers,
cues.zh: 里面都是黑客，

cues.en: people who loved programming, loved exploring what they could do with computers,
cues.zh: 他们热爱编程，喜欢探索计算机能做些什么，

cues.en: and they had developed
cues.zh: 而且他们已经开发出

cues.en: a complete operating system entirely written there,
cues.zh: 一套完整的操作系统，全都是在那里编写的。

cues.en: and I became one of the team that continued to improve the operating system adding new capabilities
cues.zh: 我成了团队的一员，继续改进这套操作系统，添加新功能。

cues.en: that was my job and I loved it we all loved it that's why we were doing it
cues.zh: 那就是我的工作，我很喜欢。我们都很喜欢，所以我们才这么做。

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 并且

cues.en: we called our system the incompatible
cues.zh: 我们把我们的系统称为“不兼容

cues.en: time sharing system,
cues.zh: 分时系统”（ITS），

cues.en: which is an example of the playful spirit
cues.zh: 这就是一种嬉戏精神的体现，

cues.en: which defines a hacker. Hackers are people who enjoy playful cleverness.
cues.zh: 而这种精神正定义了黑客。黑客就是那些享受“顽皮的机智”的人。

cues.en: Well, it first started going wrong as the outside world started pressuring us to have passwords. We didn't have any passwords on our computer.
cues.zh: 事情最初开始变味，是外界开始向我们施压，要求设置密码。我们的电脑以前根本没有任何密码。

cues.en: And the reason was that the hackers who'd originally designed the system
cues.zh: 原因在于，最初设计这个系统的黑客们

cues.en: realized
cues.zh: 早就意识到，

cues.en: that passwords were a way that the administrators could control all the users.
cues.zh: 密码其实是管理员用来控制所有用户的一种手段。

cues.en: And they didn't want to build
cues.zh: 他们不想构建

cues.en: tools, locks and keys for the administrators to control them. So they just didn't do it, they left that out.
cues.zh: 工具、锁和钥匙让管理员来控制它们。所以他们干脆没做，把这些略过了。

cues.en: And we had the philosophy that whoever is sitting at the computer should be able to do whatever he wants,
cues.zh: 我们的理念是，坐在电脑前的人想做什么就能做什么，

cues.en: and somebody else who was there yesterday shouldn't be controlling what you do today.
cues.zh: 而昨天在场的某个人不应该控制你今天做什么。

cues.en: When they put passwords onto one of the machines at MIT,
cues.zh: 当他们给MIT的一台机器加上密码时，

cues.en: I and a bunch of other hackers didn't like it. I decided to try a subversive sort of hack.
cues.zh: 我和一群其他黑客不喜欢这样。我决定尝试一种颠覆性的黑客手段。

cues.en: I figured out how to decode the passwords so by looking at the database of encoded
cues.zh: 我找到了破解密码的方法，这样只要查看数据库里编码后的

cues.en: passwords I could figure out what each person would actually type to log in.
cues.zh: 密码，我就能知道每个人登录时实际会输入什么。

cues.en: And so I sent messages to people saying
cues.zh: 于是我给大家发消息说：

cues.en: Hello, I see that you've chosen the password mumble, whatever it was. How about if you do as I do, just type enter for your password? It's much shorter, much easier to type.
cues.zh: 你好，我看到你选的密码是 mumble，还是别的什么来着。要不跟我一样，把密码直接设成回车？这样短多了，也好输入。

cues.en: And of course with this message I was implicitly telling them that the security was really just a joke.
cues.zh: 当然，这条消息也在暗示他们，所谓的安全措施根本就是个笑话。

cues.en: Anyway, but in addition I was letting them in on this hack And eventually, a fifth of all the users on that computer joined me in using just enter
cues.zh: 不管怎样，我还把这个小伎俩告诉了他们，最后那台机器上有五分之一的用户跟我一样，只用回车键

cues.en: as their passwords.
cues.zh: 来当密码。

cues.en: Where did the ideas that led to what it is now called open source, where... How did that begin? Who who began that? Well, actually began with the start of computers because at that time software was just passed around between people.
cues.zh: 孕育出如今所谓“开源”的那些理念，究竟源自何处……它是如何开始的？又是谁开创的？其实，这一切始于计算机诞生之初，因为那时软件就是在人与人之间互相传阅的。

cues.en: And I think it was only like in the late seventies,
cues.zh: 我认为直到七十年代末、

cues.en: early eighties
cues.zh: 八十年代初，

cues.en: that people started really closing up their software and saying, no, you can never get a look at the source code, you can't change the software even if it's necessary
cues.zh: 大家才真正开始封闭自己的软件，并且说：不行，你们绝不能看源码，就算为了适配你自己的应用必须修改，

cues.en: for you to fix it for your own application.
cues.zh: 你也不能改动这套软件。

cues.en: And,
cues.zh: 而且，

cues.en: you can actually blame some of that on Microsoft. They were one of the real pioneers of the proprietary
cues.zh: 你其实可以把其中一部分归咎于 Microsoft。他们是专有

cues.en: software model.
cues.zh: 软件模式的真正先驱之一。

cues.en: In the mid nineteen seventies, a group of hackers and computer hobbyists in Silicon Valley formed the Homebrew Computer Club. In the club's 01/31/1976
cues.zh: 20 世纪 70 年代中期，硅谷的一群黑客和电脑爱好者成立了家酿计算机俱乐部。在俱乐部 1976 年 1 月 31 日的

cues.en: newsletter,
cues.zh: 通讯中，

cues.en: Bill Gates of the recently formed Microsoft
cues.zh: 当时刚成立不久的 Microsoft 的 Bill Gates

cues.en: wrote an open letter to the community
cues.zh: 写了一封致社区的公开信，

cues.en: where he made a point by point argument for the relatively new concept of proprietary software.
cues.zh: 他在信中逐条论证了当时相对较新的专有软件概念。

cues.en: Up to that point, the practice of computer users had been to freely pass around software with not much thought given to its ownership.
cues.zh: 在那之前，电脑用户一直习惯随意分享软件，几乎不考虑软件的所有权。

cues.en: Known as an open letter to hobbyists, Bill Gates writes, To me, the most critical thing in the hobby market right now is the lack of good courses, books, and software itself.
cues.zh: 这封信后来被称为《致爱好者的公开信》。比尔·盖茨写道：“在我看来，目前爱好者市场最缺的，就是优质的课程、书籍和软件。”

cues.en: Without good software and an owner who understands programming, a hobby computer is wasted.
cues.zh: 没有优质软件，也没有懂编程的主人，爱好电脑就失去了意义。

cues.en: Will quality software be written for the hobby market?
cues.zh: 会有人为爱好者市场编写优质软件吗？

cues.en: Gates goes on to write:
cues.zh: 盖茨接着写道：

cues.en: positive. Two surprising things are apparent, however. One, most of these users never bought BASIC, and two, the amount of royalties we have received from sales to hobbyists makes the time spent on Altair BASIC worth less than $2 an hour. Why is this? As the majority of hobbyists must be aware, most of you steal your software.
cues.zh: 很正面。然而，有两件令人惊讶的事显而易见。第一，这些用户大多数从未购买过 BASIC；第二，我们从爱好者销售中收到的版税，折算下来在 Altair BASIC 上投入的时间每小时还不到 2 美元。为什么会这样？正如大多数爱好者心里都清楚的那样，你们大多数人都在偷窃软件。

cues.en: Hardware must be paid for, but software is something to share. Who cares if the people who worked on it get paid? Is this fair? One thing you don't do by stealing software is get back at MITTS for some problem you may have had. MITTS doesn't make money selling software.
cues.zh: 硬件必须付钱买，软件却成了拿来共享的东西。谁在乎那些开发软件的人有没有拿到报酬呢？这公平吗？你们盗版软件，并不能报复你们可能对 MITS 产生的不满。MITS 靠卖软件根本赚不到钱。

cues.en: One thing you do do is prevent good software from being written. Who can afford to do professional work for nothing? What hobbyist can put three man years into programming, finding all bugs, documenting documenting his his product, product, and distribute it for free? The fact is no one besides us has invested a lot of money in hobby software. What about the guys who resell Altair Basic? Aren't they making money on hobby software?
cues.zh: 你们做的一件事，就是阻止好软件的诞生。谁能无偿地做专业工作？哪个爱好者能投入三年时间编程、找出所有bug、为自己的产品写文档，然后免费分发？事实是，除了我们，没人往爱好者软件上投过那么多钱。那转售Altair Basic的那些人呢？他们不就是在靠爱好者软件赚钱吗？你们做的一件事，就是阻止好软件的诞生。谁能无偿地做专业工作？哪个爱好者能投入三年时间编程、找出所有bug、为自己的产品写文档，然后免费分发？事实是，除了我们，没人往爱好者软件上投过那么多钱。那转售Altair Basic的那些人呢？他们不就是在靠爱好者软件赚钱吗？

cues.en: Yes. But those who have been reported to us may lose in the end. They are the ones who give hobbyists a bad name and should be kicked out of any club meeting they show up at. I would appreciate letters from anyone who wants to pay up or has a suggestion or comment. Signed Bill Gates, general partner,
cues.zh: 是的。但我们举报过的那些人，最终可能会败诉。他们让爱好者蒙羞，出现在任何俱乐部聚会上都该被赶出去。欢迎愿意付款，或有建议和意见的人来信。署名：Bill Gates，普通合伙人，

cues.en: Microsoft.
cues.zh: Microsoft。

cues.en: In the late seventies and early nineteen eighties, Richard Stallman was doing artificial intelligence research and coding at the MIT artificial intelligence lab.
cues.zh: 七十年代末到八十年代初，Richard Stallman 在 MIT 人工智能实验室从事人工智能研究和编程。

cues.en: Richard had a number of negative experiences during that period which soured him on the whole idea of commercial software. Such as?
cues.zh: 在那段时期，Richard 经历了许多不如意的事，这让他对商业软件彻底失去了好感。比如呢？

cues.en: Some code that he wanted to work on and wanted to fix was locked up,
cues.zh: 有些他想改、想修的代码被封锁了，

cues.en: and he couldn't get the company that owned the code to let him fix it, even though it would have been to their advantage to do so. And that put me into a moral dilemma, you see, because
cues.zh: 哪怕修好对公司有利，那家拥有代码的公司也根本不让他去修。你看，这让我陷入了道德困境，因为

cues.en: to get one of the modern computers of the day, which was the early eighties,
cues.zh: 想要用上当时（也就是 80 年代初）的现代计算机，

cues.en: you would have to get a proprietary operating system.
cues.zh: 你就必须用专有操作系统。

cues.en: The developers of those systems didn't share with other people. Instead, they tried to control the users, dominate the users, restrict them,
cues.zh: 那些系统的开发者不愿和别人分享。相反，他们试图控制用户、支配用户、限制用户，

cues.en: saying, to get this system you have to sign a promise you won't share with anybody else.
cues.zh: 说，想拿到这个系统，你得签一份承诺，保证不跟任何其他人分享。

cues.en: And to me that was essentially a promise to be a bad person, to betray the rest of the world, cut myself off from society, from the cooperating community.
cues.zh: 对我来说，那本质上就是承诺做一个坏人，背叛世界上的其他人，把自己从社会、从协作共同体中割裂出去。

cues.en: And I had already experienced what happened when other people did that to us when they refused to share with us because they had signed these contracts
cues.zh: 而我已经经历过别人这样对我们时发生了什么——他们因为签了这些合同而拒绝和我们分享，

cues.en: and it hurt the whole lab kept us from doing useful things before
cues.zh: 这伤害了整个实验室，之前还让我们没法做有用的事，

cues.en: so
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: I just wasn't going to do that. I felt this is wrong. I am not going to live this way.
cues.zh: 我就是不打算那么做。我觉得这是错的。我不会那样生活。

cues.en: And from experiences like this, he developed a profound hostility to the idea of intellectual property and software.
cues.zh: 从这样的经历中，他对知识产权和软件的理念产生了强烈的敌意。

cues.en: He eventually acted this out by founding the Free Software Foundation.
cues.zh: 后来，他创立了自由软件基金会，把这种想法付诸行动。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: I look for another alternative and I realized
cues.zh: 我开始寻找另一种选择，并意识到

cues.en: I was an operating system developer.
cues.zh: 我是个操作系统开发者。

cues.en: If I were to develop
cues.zh: 如果我开发

cues.en: another operating system and
cues.zh: 另一个操作系统，然后

cues.en: then as the author encourage everyone to share it, say everyone you come and get it, use this, form a new community,
cues.zh: 作为作者，我鼓励大家分享它，告诉大家：「来拿去用，加入进来，建立一个新的社区。」

cues.en: not only could I give myself away to keep using computers out betraying other people, but I give it to everybody else too. Everybody would have a way out of that moral dilemma.

cues.zh: 下一个重大事件是我直接参与其中的。

cues.en: I wrote a paper called The Cathedral and the Bazaar, which was my observations,
cues.zh: 我写了一篇论文叫《大教堂与集市》，那是我的一些观察，

cues.en: my anthropological
cues.zh: 是我对人类学式的

cues.en: analysis
cues.zh: 分析

cues.en: of what it was that made the open source world work. We didn't call it that then. We're using the term free software primarily.
cues.zh: 分析究竟是什么让开源世界运转起来。当时我们还不这么叫，我们主要用的是“自由软件”这个词。

cues.en: So it was my observation of what made the free software world work and why
cues.zh: 所以，我观察了自由软件世界如何运作，以及我们为什么

cues.en: we were able to produce extremely high quality software
cues.zh: 能够开发出质量极高的软件

cues.en: in spite of constantly violating all of the standard rules of software engineering.
cues.zh: 尽管我们一直在违反软件工程的所有标准规则。

cues.en: In that paper, I was setting up a contrast between two different styles of development, two opposed styles of development.
cues.zh: 在那篇文章中，我对比了两种不同、相互对立的开发方式。

cues.en: One, which is the conventional
cues.zh: 一种是传统的

cues.en: closed
cues.zh: 封闭式

cues.en: development style which I I called the cathedral style.
cues.zh: 开发方式，我称之为大教堂式开发。

cues.en: In that one, have tight specification of objectives, small project groups which are run-in a fairly hierarchical
cues.zh: 在那一种模式中，目标明确而严格，项目团队规模小，且以相当层级化

cues.en: authoritarian
cues.zh: 集权专断的

cues.en: manner.
cues.zh: 方式运作。

cues.en: And you have long release intervals.
cues.zh: 而且发布周期很长。

cues.en: On the other hand, what I identified as happening in the Linux world was a much more peer to peer decentralized
cues.zh: 另一方面，我发现 Linux 世界里发生的事情更像是一种点对点的、去中心化的

cues.en: market or bizarre like style, in which you have very short release intervals and constant solicitation of feedback from people who are formally outside the project. A very intense peer
cues.zh: 集市风格，发布周期极短，并不断向项目编制之外的人征求反馈。还有非常密集的同行

cues.en: review process.
cues.zh: 评审流程。

cues.en: And the startling thing was that the more I looked at this, the more it seemed that trading away all the supposed advantages
cues.zh: 令人惊讶的是，我越研究这一点，就越觉得：放弃传统闭源开发的所有所谓优势，

cues.en: of conventional closed development for that one single advantage of massive independent peer review actually seemed to win, actually seemed to get you good results.
cues.zh: 换取大规模独立同行评审这一个优势，实际上似乎更胜一筹，确实能带来好结果。

cues.zh: 参与

cues.zh: 于是，网景转向开源，本质上是为了对抗微软，

cues.en: which was
cues.zh: 微软当时

cues.en: giving away
cues.zh: 免费提供

cues.en: Internet Explorer,
cues.zh: Internet Explorer，

cues.en: but not letting anyone else have the source code, not letting companies collaborate.
cues.zh: 却不让其他人获取源代码，也不让公司之间协作。

cues.en: Working as part of the Salesforce, I got a good I got a good idea of why people bought our software and what it took to make our software successful in the marketplace against competitive products.
cues.zh: 在 Salesforce 工作期间，我逐渐了解了人们为什么购买我们的软件，以及要让我们的软件在市场上胜过竞品，需要做到什么。

cues.en: However, the problem was... We were saying is that is that as time went on,
cues.zh: 不过，问题在于……我们发现，随着时间推移，

cues.en: our software
cues.zh: 我们的软件

cues.en: was,
cues.zh: 开始

cues.en: being competed against by other people's software, particularly Microsoft.
cues.zh: 受到其他公司的软件，尤其是微软软件的竞争。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.zh: 当时真正的问题在于，他们担心微软会垄断浏览器市场，并进而利用这种垄断地位

cues.zh: 和 HTML 这些 Web 赖以生存的标准。

cues.zh: 一旦他们把

cues.zh: 这些标准变成绑定用户的工具，

cues.zh: 他们就能利用这种控制权把 Netscape 赶出服务器市场，而那才是 Netscape 真正赚钱的地方。我担心的是，随着时间的推移，

cues.en: viable in the marketplace.
cues.zh: 在市场上可行。

cues.zh: Netscape 的发布发生在 1998 年初。后来有人告诉我，

cues.zh: 当时我完全不知道，

cues.en: that it came about as a direct result of the right people having read The Cathedral and the Bazaar.
cues.zh: 这件事的直接起因，是合适的人读了《大教堂与集市》。

cues.en: The Cathedral and The Bazaar,
cues.zh: 《大教堂与集市》，

cues.en: the paper by Eric Raymond,
cues.zh: Eric Raymond 写的那篇文章，

cues.en: was an...
cues.zh: 是一个……

cues.zh: 对 Netscape

cues.zh: 决定发布源代码产生了重大影响。这让我大为震惊。我并没有真正准备好接受这个想法：即使是无意中，我也在改变世界。

cues.zh: 然而，这绝不是促成该决定的

cues.en: on that decision,
cues.zh: 唯一影响因素，

cues.en: and not necessarily the most important one when when all is said and done.

cues.en: As I said, Netscape
cues.zh: 正如我所说，Netscape

cues.zh: 早在大家听说 Eric 的论文之前，Netscape 就已经在讨论开源代码的事了。

cues.zh: 当时听过报告的人之一，就是 O'Reilly Associates 的 Tim O'Reilly。

cues.en: And, he thought it was pretty intriguing.
cues.zh: 而且，他觉得这挺有意思的。

cues.zh: 他便邀请我去他的第一届 Perl 大会上演讲，那是在那年晚些时候，也就是 97 年的秋天。

cues.en: And apparently what happened, I was told later, although I had no idea this was happening at the time,
cues.zh: 据我后来得知，事情的发展是这样的——尽管当时我对此一无所知——

cues.en: is that some people from Netscape actually heard
cues.zh: Netscape 的一些人确实听了

cues.en: the the paper at the Pearl Conference
cues.zh: 我在 Perl 大会上的那篇论文演讲，

cues.en: and took those ideas back to Netscape and they kind of lit a fire there.
cues.zh: 并把这些想法带回了 Netscape，在公司内部引起了不小的轰动。

cues.en: The role of my paper was essentially to make the internal case at Netscape,
cues.zh: 我的论文本质上是在网景内部做论证，

cues.en: to make the business case for why Netscape should release its source code.
cues.zh: 为网景为何应该公开其源代码提供商业依据。

cues.zh: 这篇论文叫《网景源代码作为网景产品》。

cues.en: A strange title, essentially the the what the title meant was that
cues.zh: 标题有点奇怪，本质上这个标题的意思是

cues.en: in my opinion, we we needed to to think of source code not just as something that was used in creating our products, but as something that was a product in its own right.
cues.zh: 在我看来，我们需要把源代码不只当作用来创造产品的东西，而是把它本身也当作一种产品。

cues.en: Something that customers might use, other people might use.
cues.zh: 一些客户可能会用，其他人也可能会用。

cues.zh: 接着我思考，如果我们开放产品源代码，可能会有哪些商业模式。

cues.zh: 我们该怎么授权？

cues.en: How do we, how do we,
cues.zh: 我们该怎么，我们该怎么，

cues.en: sell products in this environment?
cues.zh: 在这种环境下销售产品？

cues.zh: 然后我研究了竞争对手，尤其是微软。

cues.en: What would they be likely to do if we released source code? Was there some way they could use our source code against us? I used Eric's paper as an example of how distributed development could work, how a company could develop software not just using their own people but also working
cues.zh: 如果我们开放源代码，他们可能会怎么做？他们能不能利用我们的源代码来对付我们？我用埃里克的论文举例，说明分布式开发可以怎样运作，以及一家公司如何开发软件，不只依靠自己的员工，还能与

cues.zh: 互联网上的人合作。

cues.en: And I... That's why I included a reference to Eric's paper in in my paper.
cues.zh: 所以我……这就是为什么我在论文里引用了 Eric 的论文。

cues.en: Once my paper was circulated,
cues.zh: 我的论文一旦传阅开来，

cues.en: the people who read my paper would naturally enough find a reference to Eric's paper and and read that as well. And who was involved in making that happen in Netscape?
cues.zh: 读到的人自然就会顺着引用找到 Eric 的论文，并顺便读一读。那么 Netscape 当时是谁在推动这件事呢？

cues.en: Primarily,
cues.zh: 最关键的，

cues.en: the person who made the actual decision was Jim Barksdale.
cues.zh: 真正拍板做决定的人是 Jim Barksdale。

cues.en: And this turned out to be important later, that our big win,
cues.zh: 而事实证明，这在后来变得至关重要，我们这次大获全胜，

cues.en: the big score that gave us mainstream
cues.zh: 这一让我们走向主流、

cues.en: visibility and credibility with investors
cues.zh: 在投资人面前赢得知名度和公信力的大战果，

cues.zh: 并不是靠一群工程师自下而上的布道推动的，而是因为最高层的一位战略家看到了这种方法的潜在威力，并基本上把这种远见贯彻到了下面的每一个人。

cues.zh: 他当时是

cues.zh: 当 Netscape 决定发布源代码时，

cues.zh: 但人们把 free 这个词理解成了免费。他们以为你赚不到钱，也没法卖，这完全是错误的概念。我们想传达的是，软件是开放的，源代码是公开可得的。

cues.zh: 还有 Forsyth Institute 的 Christine Peterson

cues.zh: 也参加了，另外还有几个人。Christine Peterson 是通过电话参加的。

cues.zh: John Mad Dog Hull 也通过电话参加了。

cues.zh: 一个叫 Todd Anderson 的人也在场，他后来在 SUSE 工作过一段时间。现在负责 Penguin Computing 的 Sam Auchman 也在场。当时他是

cues.zh: 我们还是想表达源代码是公开的，并且

cues.en: it was open.
cues.zh: 它是开放的。

cues.en: Well, since the first three recipients have spoken for the open source movement,
cues.zh: 既然前三位获奖者已经谈了开源运动，

cues.en: I think I should speak about the free software movement.
cues.zh: 我想我应该谈谈自由软件运动。

cues.en: The open source movement focuses on practical advantages
cues.zh: 开源运动关注的是实际好处，

cues.en: that you can get by having a community of users who can cooperate
cues.zh: 这些好处来自一个可以协作的用户社区，

cues.en: on interchanging
cues.zh: 大家可以交换

cues.en: and improving software.
cues.zh: 并改进软件。

cues.en: I agree completely with the points they make about that.
cues.zh: 我完全同意他们在这方面的观点。

cues.en: The reason why
cues.zh: 我之所以

cues.en: my views are different, why I am in the free software movement rather than the open source movement is that I believe there's something more important at stake.
cues.zh: 观点不同，之所以我站在自由软件运动而非开源运动一边，是因为我认为还有更重要的东西攸关其中。

cues.en: That freedom
cues.zh: 那种自由

cues.en: to cooperate with other people, freedom to have a community is important for our quality of life. It's important for having a good society
cues.zh: 与他人合作的自由、拥有社群的自由，对我们的生活质量很重要。它对构建一个良好的社会也很重要

cues.en: that we can live in, and that that is, in my view, even more important
cues.zh: 这样我们才能生活其中。在我看来，这甚至比

cues.en: than having powerful and reliable software.
cues.zh: 拥有强大可靠的软件更重要。

cues.en: But I think some of the people in the free software
cues.zh: 但我觉得，自由软件阵营里有些人

cues.en: camp
cues.zh: 对商业化

cues.en: are a little scared by the commercialization.
cues.zh: 有点畏惧。

cues.en: And, you know, of course, a rebel is put off by success.
cues.zh: 你知道，叛逆者当然会对成功感到不自在。

cues.en: I think that
cues.zh: 我认为

cues.en: commercialization
cues.zh: 商业化

cues.en: is very important. We want to mainstream this software.
cues.zh: 非常重要。我们希望将这类软件推向主流。

cues.en: And I work with Richard Stallman,
cues.zh: 我经常和 Richard Stallman

cues.en: who's the
cues.zh: ——也就是自由软件界

cues.en: gray haired man of free software,
cues.zh: 德高望重的前辈——一起共事，

cues.en: on a regular basis, and I don't feel
cues.zh: 我并不觉得

cues.en: I have any philosophical
cues.zh: 我们在理念上有任何

cues.en: differences.
cues.zh: 分歧。

cues.en: Me as author of the open source definition,
cues.zh: 作为开源定义的作者，

cues.en: he is originator of free software
cues.zh: 而他是自由软件运动

cues.en: as an organized thing,
cues.zh: 的发起人，

cues.en: except for one thing. Richard wants all software to be free, and I think that free software and
cues.zh: 除了一点除外：Richard 希望所有软件都自由，而我认为自由软件与

cues.en: non free software should coexist.
cues.zh: 非自由软件应当共存。

cues.en: That's the only difference we have. We decided early on that we needed a
cues.zh: 这就是我们唯一的区别。我们很早就决定，我们需要一个

cues.en: definition, we needed a kind of meta license
cues.zh: 定义，我们需要一种元许可证

cues.en: to define the term open source. And what we came up with is a document called the open source definition. It's derived from the Debian Free Software guidelines that were originally written by Bruce Perrons.
cues.zh: 来定义开源这个词。我们最终拿出的是一份叫“开源定义”的文件。它源自 Bruce Perrons 最初编写的 Debian 自由软件指导方针。

cues.en: I'd written the original draft of that,
cues.zh: 那份初稿是我写的，

cues.en: discussed
cues.zh: 然后和

cues.en: it for a month with the Debian developers, Debian is a Linux distribution,
cues.zh: Debian 的开发者讨论了一个月，Debian 是一个 Linux 发行版，

cues.en: and made it their project policy.
cues.zh: 并把它定为他们的项目政策。

cues.en: Eric and I decided to relabel
cues.zh: 我和 Eric 决定重新命名我们为 Debian 编写的那份内容，

cues.en: what we'd written for Debian as the open source definition,
cues.zh: 把它称为“开源定义”，

cues.en: and to say open source is software that gives you a list of nine rights, which is in the open source definition.
cues.zh: 并说开源软件会赋予你九项权利，这些权利都列在开源定义里。

cues.en: The first right is free redistribution.
cues.zh: 第一项权利是自由再分发。

cues.en: This doesn't mean free as in no price, it means liberty.
cues.zh: 这里的“自由”不是指免费，而是指自由。

cues.en: You
cues.zh: 你

cues.en: have to be free to redistribute
cues.zh: 必须能够自由地把

cues.en: your software to someone else, and actually no price is a side effect you can charge for that redistribution
cues.zh: 自己的软件再分发给别人；实际上，是否收费是你的自由，

cues.en: or not.
cues.zh: 收不收费都可以。

cues.en: It has to come with source code
cues.zh: 它必须附带源代码

cues.en: so that someone can maintain
cues.zh: 这样别人才能维护

cues.en: a program
cues.zh: 程序

cues.en: if they go from a PC to a Mac for example, they can change the software.
cues.zh: 比如他们从 PC 换到 Mac 时，就能自行修改软件。

cues.en: Derived works have to be possible. If someone has to improve your program,
cues.zh: 必须允许衍生作品。如果有人想要改进你的程序，

cues.en: they
cues.zh: 他们

cues.en: should be able to distribute
cues.zh: 应该能够分发

cues.en: the result.
cues.zh: 修改后的成果。

cues.en: There's
cues.zh: 还有一条

cues.en: a provision about integrity of the author's source code, which says that
cues.zh: 关于保持作者源代码完整性的条款，它规定

cues.en: the author can sort of maintain their honor, and if you make a change, you might have to change the name of the program or mark out your change very clearly
cues.zh: 作者可以在某种程度上维护自己的声誉，如果你做了修改，可能得更改程序名称，或者非常清楚地标明你的改动

cues.en: so that your change doesn't reflect on the author.
cues.zh: 这样你的改动就不会影响到原作者的声誉。

cues.en: There is no discrimination
cues.zh: 不歧视任何人

cues.en: against people or groups.
cues.zh: 也不歧视任何群体。

cues.en: The example I usually use is you can't stop an abortion clinic or an anti abortion activist from using the software.
cues.zh: 我常用的例子是，你不能阻止堕胎诊所或反堕胎活动人士使用这个软件。

cues.en: There's no discrimination against fields of endeavor,
cues.zh: 不歧视任何领域的工作，

cues.en: and that means the software has to be usable
cues.zh: 这意味着该软件必须能用于

cues.en: in a business
cues.zh: 商业场合，

cues.en: as well as in a school.
cues.zh: 也能用于学校。

cues.en: The license has to be distributable.
cues.zh: 许可证必须可以再分发。

cues.en: In other words, I
cues.zh: 换句话说，我

cues.en: have to be able to give that license to someone and that license
cues.zh: 必须能够把该许可证交给别人，而该许可证

cues.en: then
cues.zh: 接着

cues.en: should work if that someone gives it to yet a third person.
cues.zh: 也应有效，即使那个人又把它交给第三个人。

cues.en: The license can't be specific
cues.zh: 许可证不能针对

cues.en: to a product. In other words, if I
cues.zh: 特定产品。换句话说，如果我

cues.en: distribute my software on a Red Hat system, the license can't say,
cues.zh: 在 Red Hat 系统上分发我的软件，许可证不能说：

cues.en: you can't distribute this on a SUSO or a Debian system.
cues.zh: 你不能在 SUSO 或 Debian 系统上分发这个。

cues.en: The license can't contaminate
cues.zh: 许可证不能污染

cues.en: other software,
cues.zh: 其他软件，

cues.en: so if I
cues.zh: 所以如果我

cues.en: distribute this on a CD
cues.zh: 把软件放在 CD 上

cues.en: with another program, it can't say that other program must be free, otherwise you can't distribute my software.
cues.zh: 和另一个程序一起分发，它不能说另一个程序必须是自由的，否则你就不能分发我的软件。

cues.en: And then the only other part of the open source definition is a list of licenses that were accepted
cues.zh: 开源定义唯一剩下的部分就是一份被认可的许可证列表，

cues.en: and the ones that we started with were the GPL which was actually the example
cues.zh: 我们最开始有的是 GPL，它实际上就是个范例，

cues.en: for a lot of what's in the open source definition,
cues.zh: 开源定义里很多内容都源自它，

cues.en: the BSD license, because software for BSD system preexisted
cues.zh: 还有 BSD 许可证，因为 BSD 系统的软件早于

cues.en: Linux.
cues.zh: Linux 就存在了。

cues.en: I think
cues.zh: 我认为

cues.en: the next moment that I thought was really pivotal was when the database vendors flipped over, which happened about three months sooner than I expected it to. It actually happened in late July, early August.
cues.zh: 下一个真正关键的时刻，是各大数据库厂商纷纷倒戈转向的时候，这比我的预期早了大约三个月，其实就发生在七月下旬、八月初。

cues.en: We commitments
cues.zh: 我们拿到了

cues.en: to do Tier one ports from Oracle and
cues.zh: 来自 Oracle 的一级支持移植承诺，以及

cues.en: Sybase
cues.zh: Sybase

cues.en: and the other key database vendors. And why was that critical? Because we knew that in order for the open source story to be credible,
cues.zh: 和其他核心数据库厂商的承诺。为什么这至关重要？因为我们深知，要让开源方案立得住脚，

cues.en: and especially in order for the Linux story to be credible, we'd have to get commitments from independent software vendors to do ports of their applications
cues.zh: 尤其是要让 Linux 方案真正具有可信度，就必须获得独立软件开发商的承诺，把他们的应用移植

cues.en: to these platforms.
cues.zh: 到这些平台上。

cues.en: And I was actually kind of worried. I felt that we were in a window of vulnerability between the time that we announced the open source campaign and the database vendors flipped over. That was the point at which hostile action by Microsoft or other closed source software companies,
cues.zh: 我当时其实挺担心的。我觉得，从宣布开源行动到数据库厂商转向支持开源，这段时间我们处在一个脆弱的窗口期。微软或其他闭源软件公司可能会趁机采取敌对行动，

cues.en: that was the point at which a serious marketing blitz might actually have sunk us.
cues.zh: 那时一场大规模的营销攻势可能真的会把我们击垮。

cues.en: But once the big database vendors flipped over,
cues.zh: 但等大型数据库厂商转向支持开源后，

cues.en: that opened the way for other ISVs. That started a snowball effect going. Every six months or so, I would come back to the venture capitalists and I would show them the new numbers,
cues.zh: 其他独立软件厂商也就有了进场的机会，雪球效应随之开始。每隔六个月左右，我就会去找风险投资人，给他们看最新的数据，

cues.en: showing more and more people adopting Linux, the new people porting, new users, and I'd show them our customer list.
cues.zh: 展示越来越多的人开始采用 Linux、新加入的移植团队和新用户，还会给他们看我们的客户名单。

cues.en: And our customer list was getting much more impressive. It was people like Cisco that were beginning to appear.
cues.zh: 而且我们的客户名单越来越有分量，像 Cisco 这样的公司都开始出现了。

cues.en: People like the, you know, the .com companies were starting to show up on our our customer list. And eventually, the venture capitalists,
cues.zh: 比如那些互联网泡沫时期的 dot-com 公司，也开始出现在我们的客户名单上。最终，那些风险投资人，

cues.zh: 他们一直在观望，总是在说，哎呀，我们还不能投。直到 Linus 登上了《财富》杂志的封面，开源领域确实正在发生些什么。

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 嗯，

They just got sick of hearing about Linux everywhere, and they got tired of me just, you know, showing it to them every every... At that point, almost almost every week. So they they decided it was time to invest, that there was something happening.
cues.zh: 那时候，风险投资人已经没法再忽视它了。他们听到哪里都在说 Linux，都听烦了。我也总是把它拿给他们看，每次都……那时候差不多每周都要展示一次。所以他们觉得该投资了，觉得这事确实要成了。

cues.zh: 行政

cues.zh: 工作，创立了开放源代码促进会。

cues.zh: 大概六个月后，我发现新闻里铺天盖地都是“开源”这个词，

cues.zh: 当时整个人都惊呆了。

cues.zh: 我想大概过了一年，微软当时在谈论要开放部分源代码，
